parallel.requirements: Recognized the five required fuzzing algorithms and exact EXPERIMENT_NAME: VALUE run.sh output contract from the task prompt.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Implemented AFL first, then delegated AFLFast, AFLGo, AFL++, and FairFuzz to child workers while the parent retained run.sh and commit ownership.
parallel.implementation: Completed and committed AFL, AFLFast, FairFuzz, and AFL++ work; the first AFLGo worker aborted and the replacement produced only partial/tuning work before closure.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated completed non-AFLGo modules through commits and run.sh additions, but no AFLGo requirement patch or commit was present in the final parallel git log.
parallel.verification: Child reports verified their modules, and the parent sanity-checked partial AFLGo modules, but final full run.sh verification was still pending when the run ended.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: AFLGo remained unfinished/uncommitted at agent timeout, and official testing also exposed the base AFLFuzzer add_to_queue and seed-constructor API defects.

serial.requirements: Worked from the same five-algorithm requirement set and retained the full expected-output and git-patch obligations in one main session.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all implementation, run.sh, testing, and commits in the main serial trajectory with no subagents or swarm delegation.
serial.implementation: Implemented all five requirements, including AFLGo distance, annealing, experiment, run.sh section, and requirement patch material.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Committed one requirement sequence through AFL++, with git log showing AFLGo and all other requirement commits in the final tree.
serial.verification: Ran the full agent test suite and run.sh, then parsed every requirement YAML expected output against run.sh with all matches reported.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No process timeout or missing AFLGo work remained, but official hidden tests still failed the base AFLFuzzer add_to_queue and seed-constructor API contract.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel prompt required all five fuzzers and exact deterministic output sections, and the parent delegated the four remaining algorithms including AFLGo.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial prompt had the same five-fuzzer obligation and the serial run later had commits for all five requirements, including AFLGo.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both runs recognized the full requirement set, but serial carried AFLGo to a committed requirement while parallel left AFLGo incomplete after the aborted child chain.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a swarm for AFLFast, AFLGo, AFL++, and FairFuzz while the parent kept run.sh and commits, then reassigned AFLGo after the initial child was aborted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one main trajectory with no delegation or subagents and committed each requirement in order from one workspace owner.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a child lifecycle dependency for AFLGo; serial avoided handoff and child completion dependencies by keeping ownership local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel child brief named each requirement YAML, exact outputs, and the no-run.sh/no-git boundary, so the reviewed problem is not missing task context.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial needed no cross-agent interface handoff; the main session kept the requirement files, implementation files, run.sh, and commits in one context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No retained context/interface label is supported; the contrast is lifecycle completion of AFLGo, not missing child instructions or conflicting handoffs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel committed AFL, AFLFast, FairFuzz, and AFL++ but had no AFLGo commit in the final git log and showed AFLGo modules still untracked during recovery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial committed AFLGo as a requirement commit and then committed the remaining requirement work through AFL++.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete implementation difference is missing committed AFLGo delivery in parallel versus complete serial AFLGo implementation and patch material.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The first parallel swarm returned three completed modules and one aborted AFLGo child, after which a replacement child began but did not return a finished AFLGo experiment.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main session completed work without child joins and reached final verification in the same trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the initial AFLGo result before finalization; serial had no corresponding child result lifecycle failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel shared the workspace across agents but the observed integration state was not a file collision; instead AFLGo modules remained untracked while other requirements were committed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated all requirement files and run.sh sections into the final repository, including AFLGo experiment output in run.sh.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The meaningful integration difference is incomplete AFLGo integration in parallel, not a concurrent overwrite or artifact contamination event.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had child-level verification for completed modules but the parent was still waiting for AFLGo before final full run.sh verification; official testing later failed the base AFL API contract.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran the full agent test suite and run.sh with all five expected output sections before official testing later failed the same AFL API contract.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial completed stronger whole-task self-verification including AFLGo; parallel did not reach final verification because AFLGo was still pending, while both official failures stemmed from the same AFLFuzzer API mismatch.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel round 3 recorded swarm mode, active delegation, and agent timeout after 2393 seconds for that prompt with overall failure_mode agent_timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial round 2 completed without timeout or delegation and the official run recorded failure_mode none despite failing the hidden tests.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status records make this pair both_fail: neither mode passed. The material task-solving difference is that serial reached complete five-requirement implementation and self-verification, including AFLGo, while parallel timed out after an aborted AFLGo child and incomplete replacement work. The shared official failure is explained by an ordinary AFLFuzzer API mismatch visible in both post-test logs, so the retained parallel coordination pattern is an adverse process difference but not an official pass/fail differential.
parallel_contributors: Parallel AFLGo child aborted before finalization; replacement work was still tuning and AFLGo remained uncommitted at timeout.
serial_contributors: Serial completed and committed AFLGo and all other requirements, then self-verified run.sh against all expected outputs before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both official post-test logs failed the base AFLFuzzer public API contract: add_to_queue was absent and AFLFuzzer could not be constructed with seed=42 as expected.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No official outcome difference; supported process contrast and retained parallel adverse coordination episode only.

candidates.reason: Rejected: every required algorithm had an explicit implementer in the parent or a child; AFLGo was owned even though one child aborted.
Rejected: the parent explicitly owned run.sh and commit integration; the adverse event was child termination rather than absent integration ownership.
Rejected: the parent handled final assembly and commits for completed modules; missing AFLGo assembly followed unfinished child output.
Rejected: the parent controlled the implementation to commit and verification pipeline; the unresolved point was AFLGo child lifecycle.
Rejected: productive implementation began immediately and four module implementations were delegated without waiting on one mandatory serial preflight.
Rejected: the parallel children performed implementation work, not an investigation-only phase that delayed all productive work.
Rejected: AFLGo became critical, but the directly evidenced boundary was the explicit child abortion and replacement, so this same-chain load symptom is suppressed.
Rejected: broad parallel fan-out existed, but the independent evidence points to one aborted AFLGo child and recovery chain rather than collective fan-out exhaustion.
Rejected: the AFLGo child was scoped to one requirement, and its incompletion is evidenced as abortion/replacement tuning rather than an overbroad assignment.
Rejected: the AFLGo delegation included the requirement YAML, exact expected outputs, deterministic constraints, and file deliverables; no known requirement was missing from the child brief.
Rejected: agents owned distinct requirement-scoped files and the parent owned run.sh; no incompatible cross-agent interface contract caused the observed shortfall.
Rejected: no known finding or current-file fact disappeared during transfer; the first AFLGo child did not return a completed handoff.
Rejected: returned completed child reports for AFLFast, FairFuzz, and AFL++ were usable and consumed; no oversized handoff blocked a decision.
Rejected: no receiver acted on a superseded workspace, requirement, or dependency state.
Rejected: no incompatible reports or contracts reached the parent and remained unadjudicated.
Rejected: the parent did not present or accept the whole task as complete; final response was empty and the official run timed out before closure.
Rejected: the replacement AFLGo work inherited visible partial modules and proceeded with targeted tuning rather than repeating without checkpoint state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The first parallel swarm returned the AFLGo child as aborted before it produced the needed experiment result. The parent then launched a replacement AFLGo agent and inspected partial AFLGo modules, but the workspace still showed AFLGo files untracked and the replacement was still tuning/searching when the parallel run timed out.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parallel run spent its closure window recovering AFLGo and still delivered no AFLGo requirement patch or commit before the agent timeout.
candidates.near_match_reason: No Failure Takeover is the closest rejected label, but the parent did launch a replacement AFLGo agent and inspected partial AFLGo work; the direct boundary is premature child termination.

candidates.reason: Rejected: no complete directly promotable AFLGo experiment or mutually complete component set existed before closure; the work was still being tuned.
Rejected: no child result was merged after final integrated verification without a follow-up check; final integrated verification had not occurred.
Rejected: completed AFLFast, FairFuzz, and AFL++ implementations were joined and committed, while AFLGo was not a completed retrievable implementation.
Rejected: no verifier child produced a concrete finding trapped below the parent.
Rejected: after the AFLGo abort, the parent launched a replacement AFLGo agent and inspected partial AFLGo modules.
Rejected: completed child results were inspected and used for commits, and no completed AFLGo result was available and ignored.
Rejected: the parent and replacement child actively inspected modules and ran tuning searches; there was no blind wait on an available result.
Rejected: agents wrote distinct requirement-scoped implementation files; no competing cross-file designs required reconciliation.
Rejected: no two live agents were shown editing the same source file and reconciling conflicting edits.
Rejected: no non-entry source produced or owned by one active actor was wholesale replaced by another.
Rejected: the required run.sh deliverable was controlled by the parent and not concurrently overwritten by another actor.
Rejected: no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced another actor's final-tree work or provenance.
Rejected: although agents shared a workspace, the realized issue was unfinished AFLGo child work, not an unstable shared-state provenance problem.
Rejected: no temporary file, cache, generated artifact, or process output from one actor was consumed by another as stable input.
